BENSENVILLE YARD | ELKHART 
 
 
 
 
Bensenville will be under continuous construction over the next couple of years and we will be 
issuing out Superintendent Notices to keep the employees updated on areas that they will need to 
be cautious around. 
 
(Tuesday, December 17, 2024) 
 
The Hump Pull Back and A-Lead will now have a new track alignment. 
  
There will be a new independent D–Lead south of the existing F-Lead. 
 
There is a new crossover connecting the D-Lead and C-Lead 
 
 
(Pictures on Page 2 – 4) 
Subject: Bensenville Yard Continuous Construction – January 1, 2025 
US Eastern Region  
January 1, 2025

5 
(Wednesday, November 20, 2024) 
 
ALL EMPLOYEES – Please be advised that ALL SWITCHES east of the Mannheim Bridge have wires protruding from 
ground for future installation. Be mindful of your footing around and when throwing these switches. 
 
 
 
 
(Monday, November 4, 2024) 
 
Track IM5 on the Franklin Avenue side does not have a proper walking path and employees should be mindful of their 
footing if required be on that side of the track. There are currently barriers outlining areas affected. 
 
A walking path is currently being created and an update will be issued when completed. 
 
(Wednesday, October 2, 2024) 
 
Effective, Wednesday, October 2, 2024, anyone yarding their train or working in the Intermodal Yard will be required to 
contact the trainmaster on duty at Bensenville for a briefing. 
 
New IM4 switch has been shifted north and the new IM4 track is now in service directly south of IM3 track. 
Old IM4 switch is lined for IM5. Old IM4 is now out of service.

6 
 
 
 
(Sunday, August 11, 2024) 
 
Effective, Sunday, August 11, 2024, construction will begin over by the Intermodal Container Base (PAD 4) which will 
involve the ripping up and resurfacing of the gravel and concrete. Be mindful of your surroundings while driving and walking 
through the container base.

7 
(Thursday, July 18, 2024) 
 
Effective, Thursday, July 18, 2024, Illinois Tollway will be starting their construction around the UP Bridge and West Yard. 
They will be performing work Monday through Friday every week until further notice. All employees and crews are to be 
mindful of their surrounding when heading west through Bensenville Yard.  
 
(Monday, June 27, 2024) 
 
Effective Monday, June 27, 2024, Bensenville Yard will be going through extensive construction altering the layout of the 
yard.  
 
All employees & crews that are starting their shift, as well as crews entering the yard will be required to have a job briefing 
with the Yardmaster on duty to go over current changes and what to look out for. 
 
Crews are expected to be mindful of all the heavy machinery, contracted employees and semi-trucks that will be moving 
throughout Bensenville Yard. Do not get distracted and always remember to take the safe course. 
 
 
 
(June 27, 2024) – Construction updates as follows: 
 
CHANGES TO EXISTING TRACKS 
• PBD/PBA & PB2 – Will be shifted to the new alignment. 
• PB1 – Will be going out of service and removed completely. 
• PB3 & PB4 – Will continue to use the old lead for access on the West end. 
 
 
NEW CHANGES 
• New IMS Departure, Arrival, and IMS 1 will be in-service post-shutdown. 
• The new IMS Departure Track will tie into the A Lead. 
• The new IMS Arrival Track will tie into the West Yard Lead. 
 
Pictures of the changes below 
 
 
 
(April 4, 2024) – New maps are available of Bensenville Yard. If you require a map, please reach out to the Train 
Clerks at the East End Lunchroom or contact any manager on duty. 
 
**WALKING CONDITIONS** 
There is still extensive construction throughout Bensenville Yard. There will be possible exposed debris and 
uneven footing close to where construction is happening. It is important to be mindful of your surroundings at all 
times.

8 
While out in the yard if you happen to notice any hazards, contact your local manager and advise of the hazards so 
it can be updated and broadcast to everyone. 
 
*** We will continue to update this Superintendent Notice as more changes are made that impact employees in the yard *** 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Joshua Pennington 
Superintendent of Operations 
US Eastern Region

All T&E employees operating a Company vehicle, truck, ATV or Kubota are required to complete the Vehicle Inspection 
Form prior to moving/operating said vehicle.  Vehicle Inspection Forms are to be turned into the clerk at the east end 
lunchroom or once installed the lockbox at the West Doublewide trailer. Failure to complete the required document and/or 
report damage to a Company vehicle may result in disciplinary action. 
 
Vehicle Driving Instructions 
 
1) Prior to the movement of a vehicle, the driver must conduct a 360-degree safety walk around of the vehicle to identify 
potential obstructions or hazards. 
 
2) Special care and attention is required when parking, turning or backing up motor vehicles. Use pull-through parking if 
available. When pull-through parking is unavailable, unless it is unsafe to do so, back vehicles into parking locations. 
 
3) If there is a passenger in the vehicle, the driver must ensure that the passenger exits the vehicle and assists in guiding 
the driver when backing up. 
 
4) If backing up and no other employee is available, prior to and during the movement, the driver must ensure they are 
aware of all potential obstructions in their path in order to avoid contact. 
 
It is the Operator’s responsibility upon relieving themselves of the vehicle, to make sure all trash and debris is 
removed from the vehicle. 
 
 
Kubota Procedures 
 
Operating Rules: 
• Seatbelts are required at all times 
• Follow posted speed limits 
• Lights are to remain on at all times while in operations 
• Any damage or incident is to be reported to the Trainmaster Immediately 
• Any and all alterations to company vehicles is prohibited 
• Inspection sheet is to be filled out every shift before use and submitted using the proper procedures 
• DIESEL only – if there are any issues, please contact the Mechanical Foreman on duty 
Subject: Vehicle & Kubota Inspections, Driving Instructions, & Procedures Revised: 
(Removal of IY11 & IY21 – With Less Than 1 Year Employee Driving Kubota)

Effective immediately, all crews are instructed to call the Trainmaster or Yardmaster on duty when they arrive at the

safe.

day.

request where a cab will be needed.

Effective immediately, all daylight RCO jobs will be required to drain the locomotive main reservoirs on the RCO units 
daily at the beginning of their shift. The process is outlined below. Once completed, report to the Yardmaster for 
tracking purposes.  
Units/Product Affected: All RCL equipped locomotives  
Description: RCL Locomotive Winter Operation   
Action Required: All RCL equipped locomotive must have both Main Reservoirs drained daily by the T&E Operating Crew. 
Both Main Reservoir Drain Valve must be placed in the Automatic Mode at all time to keep draining the accumulated 
moisture.  
AUTOMATIC MODE POSITION 
Turning the Main Reservoir Drain Valve Handle fully to the LEFT will place the Drain Valve in Automatic Mode (by turning 
the handle fully to the left the stem of the valve will come out, which is a brass-threaded shaft).  
MANUAL DRAINING MODE 
Turning the Main Reservoir Drain Valve Handle to the RIGHT will open the drain valve and allow moisture to drain from 
the Main Reservoir. When moisture as finished escaping from the Main Reservoir, turn the Handle fully to the LEFT to 
place the Main Reservoir Drain Valve back into Automatic Mode.  
CLOSED MANUAL MODE 
Turning the Main Reservoir Drain Valve Handle fully to the RIGHT will place the Drain Valve in Manual mode in the 
CLOSED position and no moisture can escape (by turning the handle to the Right, the stem of the valve will go in and the 
brass-threaded shaft will be flush with the handle).     !!! DO NOT USE THIS POSITION!!!
